head: A tiny shop in the desert
fed a whole nation.
slides.sub: How Haldiram's turned a local snack into a packaged giant.

image.label: A small sweet shop in an old desert town at dawn
image.brief: 1930년대 라자스탄 비카네르의 좁은 골목, 새벽빛 속 작은 과자 가게. 큰 솥과 노란 부지아 더미. 따뜻한 사막 톤. 로고나 간판 글자 없음.

head: Bikaner had
a snack everyone made.
body: Bhujia, a crunchy fried snack made from spiced gram flour, was sold all over Bikaner. Every family and every stall had its own version.
A story often told: one young shopkeeper made his thinner and crispier than the rest.

image.label: Hands pressing thin strands of dough into hot oil
image.brief: 뜨거운 기름 위로 가느다란 반죽 가닥을 눌러 짜는 손. 인물 얼굴은 보이지 않게. 연기와 황금빛 조명.

slides.label: the year Ganga Bishan Agarwal, known as Haldiram, opened his shop
body: It was a small counter in a small city. Customers came for one thing, and they came back for it. The name on the shop came from his nickname.

image.label: A paper cone of bhujia on an old wooden counter
image.brief: 낡은 나무 계산대 위 종이 고깔에 담긴 부지아. 1930년대 인도 시장 분위기. 상표 없음.

head: The family moved.
The recipe went with them.
body: Over the following decades, his sons and grandsons opened shops in Kolkata, Nagpur and Delhi.
Each city added sweets and new snacks. But a shop can only serve the people who walk past its door.

image.label: A busy Indian city street with a crowded sweet shop
image.brief: 1970~80년대 인도 대도시 거리, 손님이 몰린 과자 가게. 인물은 실루엣 위주. 간판 글자 없음.

head: Fresh snacks travel badly.
That was the limit.
body: Fried snacks go stale and soak up moisture. Sold loose from big jars, they had to be eaten close to where they were made.
Most namkeen makers in India stayed local for exactly this reason.

image.label: Rows of open glass jars of snacks in a small shop
image.brief: 작은 가게 선반의 뚜껑 열린 유리병들, 습한 공기 속 스낵. 소박하고 정겨운 톤.

head: Loyal crowds, one city.
How do you grow?
body: Your snacks are famous locally. India's cities are growing, and more people shop in stores far from your counter.

options.text: Stay a premium sweet shop and open a few more branches
options.feedback: Safe and profitable, but growth is limited to wherever you can build a shop. Keep swiping.

options.text: Seal traditional snacks in packets and sell them through stores everywhere
options.feedback: This means new machines, consistent recipes and a sales network, with heavy upfront cost. Keep swiping.

options.text: Copy Western potato chips, the snack that looks modern
options.feedback: It would mean fighting global brands on their own product. Keep swiping.

image.label: A crossroads between a sweet shop and a delivery truck
image.brief: 작은 과자 가게와 출발하는 배송 트럭이 갈림길에 선 구도. 1980년대 인도 도시.

head: The same old snack,
in a new packet.
body: The family businesses invested in factories and sealed packaging. Bhujia and dozens of other namkeen could now sit on a shelf for weeks and taste the same in any town.
Small grocery stores across India started stocking them, and exports followed to many countries.

image.label: Factory line filling sealed snack packets
image.brief: 밀봉 포장된 스낵 봉지가 흘러가는 공장 라인. 실제 브랜드 디자인 없이 단색 봉지로.

head: Global brands arrived.
Local taste held on.
body: When multinational snack makers expanded in India, many expected local players to fade. Instead, Haldiram's stayed strong in traditional snacks.
The business grew under separate family-run companies by region, yet the name became known nationwide.

image.label: A grocery shelf where traditional snacks crowd out chips
image.brief: 인도 동네 식료품점 선반, 전통 스낵 봉지가 감자칩 봉지보다 많이 진열된 모습. 로고 없음.

head: Keep the taste.
Change how it travels.
body: Haldiram's didn't abandon what customers loved to look modern. It kept a local flavor that global rivals couldn't easily copy.
What changed was the system: standard recipes, factories and packaging that let one shop's product reach millions.

image.label: A paper cone and a sealed packet side by side
image.brief: 옛 종이 고깔과 현대식 밀봉 봉지가 나란히 놓인 정물. 같은 부지아가 담겨 있음.

head: Your best product may
just need to travel.
body: Growth doesn't always need a new product. Sometimes it needs a way to deliver the old one anywhere, the same every time.
**Try it today:** what do customers love that only works near you? What would it take to make it consistent and portable?

image.label: Snack packets loaded onto a truck at sunrise
image.brief: 해 뜰 무렵 트럭에 실리는 스낵 상자들. 희망적인 황금빛 톤. 로고 없음.

factChecks.note: 1937년 비카네르(라자스탄)에서 Ganga Bishan Agarwal(별명 'Haldiram')이 작은 가게를 연 것은 Haldiram's 공식 연혁과 주요 언론 보도 기준입니다. 연도와 이름을 회사 자료로 확인하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1937년 비카네르 창업 확인.
그가 더 가늘고 바삭한 부지아를 만들었다는 이야기는 회사가 전하는 창업 일화입니다. 카드에는 'a story often told'로 표시했고, 원료(모스콩 가루 등) 세부는 넣지 않았습니다.
콜카타(1950년대), 나그푸르(1970년대), 델리(1980년대 초) 확장 시기는 자료마다 조금씩 다릅니다. 카드에는 연도 없이 도시 이름만 적었습니다. 정확한 연도를 확인한 뒤 필요하면 추가하세요.
가족이 지역별로 나뉜 별도 회사(델리, 나그푸르, 콜카타 등)로 운영되어 왔고 상표 분쟁이 있었다는 점은 언론 보도로 확인하세요. 최근 델리·나그푸르 사업 통합 보도는 카드에 넣지 않았습니다.
매출 규모, 해외 판매국 수, 외국 투자자 지분 인수 및 기업가치 보도는 수치가 자료마다 달라 모두 넣지 않았습니다. '수많은 국가로 수출'은 정성 표현으로만 적었습니다.
글로벌 스낵 브랜드가 인도에 진출한 뒤에도 Haldiram's가 전통 스낵(namkeen)에서 강자로 남았다는 내용은 업계 보도 기준의 정성 표현입니다. 시장점유율 수치는 넣지 않았습니다.

sources.text: Pavitra Kumar, Bhujia Barons: The Untold Story of How Haldiram Built a ₹5000-crore Empire (Penguin, 2016)
The Economic Times and Mint coverage of Haldiram's family businesses and growth (2010s–2020s)
